purpose: Self-contained on-demand review and evidence validation. No automatic certification, remediation, or release.

applicability_rules.all: Always in scope; the inventory may establish that individual subcases are absent, but the control itself cannot be excluded.
applicability_rules.any_of: Applicable if any named feature is true. Unknown if none is true and at least one is null or absent. Not applicable only if all are false and the assessment supplies evidence and rationale.
applicability_rules.unknown: Never silently skip unknown applicability. Individual controls may have a documented narrower applicability decision than their module; module selection is a discovery aid, not an automatic pass.

risk_based.meaning: The project owner sets a justified review interval for each applicable risk. A missing interval or assessed_at/valid_until prevents a current pass. Relevant changes invalidate evidence immediately, irrespective of the interval.

rules: Research never grants a release pass.
Unknown applicability or missing evidence for potentially critical controls prevents a green gate.
Only a designated gate owner can accept an exception or authorize release.
A pass requires current validation for every selected control or current evidenced inapplicability. Exception acceptance is outside this tool and does not grant eligibility.
Passing this catalog is scoped assurance, not a legal certification or a claim of complete security.

controls.title: Accountable ownership
controls.expected_outcome: Product, operations, security and support ownership are identified.

research.method: Inspect ownership records, escalation contacts and support routes.

validation.method: Confirm named roles and working escalation paths without sending messages.

controls.title: System inventory
controls.expected_outcome: Repositories, deployments, domains, APIs, data stores, queues and jobs have an inventory, including delegated and client-direct services.

research.method: Compare architecture, infrastructure definitions and available deployment inventories. Trace browser/mobile clients to provider URLs as well as owned servers; record direct database APIs, auth, storage, realtime and alternate ingress. Identify shared quotas, billable dependencies and which provider/application layer owns each protection.

validation.method: Reconcile declared services against authorized deployed metadata and client destination configuration. Account for provider-generated routes and default exposure even when no application route exists; reconcile discrepancies without brute-force discovery.
evidence_required: Service/destination inventory with owner, ingress, provider defaults and shared resource dependencies; unknown deployed configuration stays explicit.

controls.false_positive_guidance: A public API key or direct browser-to-provider design is not itself a secret leak or defect. Inventory intentional public and private services without requiring an owned gateway.

controls.title: Audience and geography
controls.expected_outcome: Intended ages, audiences, supported regions and restricted markets are explicit.

research.method: Inspect product positioning, onboarding, distribution and business records.

validation.method: Obtain owner confirmation of audience and market assumptions.

controls.title: Data classification
controls.expected_outcome: Sensitive data classes and their locations are known.

research.method: Inspect schemas, forms, integrations and redacted field definitions.

validation.method: Reconcile collected fields with a classified data inventory.

controls.title: Data-flow map
controls.expected_outcome: Collection, processing, third-party transfers, logging and backup flows are documented.

research.method: Trace data paths in source and configuration without collecting actual personal records.

validation.method: Check representative paths against authorized runtime/configuration evidence.

controls.title: Obligation applicability
controls.expected_outcome: Applicable legal, contractual and platform obligations have documented factual predicates.

research.method: Research current primary sources and compare audience, geography, data and business facts.

validation.method: Resolve applicability assumptions with an accountable owner or qualified specialist.

controls.title: Threat boundaries
controls.expected_outcome: Trust boundaries and credible confidentiality, integrity, availability and financial-abuse cases are identified.

research.method: Inspect architecture and enumerate adversarial entry points and trusted decisions, including provider defaults and customer responsibilities. Model anonymous callers, cheap/free accounts, account farming and distributed clients consuming shared quotas. Ask what happens at 10,000 calls per minute, and justify workload-specific rates, concurrency, cost and blast-radius assumptions rather than treating that number as a universal test threshold.

validation.method: Reconcile abuse scenarios with the inventory and effective controls, separating data isolation from resource isolation. Walk through repeat calls, expensive reads and cross-account aggregate exhaustion, containment and recovery. Review at architecture choice and reassess authorized scope when tables, functions, routes, provider exposure or resource contracts change; a tabletop is not executed runtime proof.
evidence_required: Threat-to-control mapping for availability and financial exposure alongside data access, with provider responsibility gaps, assumptions, owners and remaining validation.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Intentional public access and documented residual exposure are not automatically vulnerabilities. Report credible uncontrolled exhaustion and unknown protection separately; data isolation alone cannot establish abuse resistance.

controls.title: Abandoned assets
controls.expected_outcome: Obsolete previews, endpoints, services and unsupported components are tracked.

research.method: Compare code references and authorized service inventories.

validation.method: Verify ownership and intended exposure of apparently orphaned assets.

controls.title: Authentication coverage
controls.expected_outcome: Every protected entry point enforces authentication at a trusted boundary.

research.method: Map protected route/API/worker authentication to the verified principal. Inspect alternate methods and middleware bypasses, and whether caller-supplied user/role/tenant or proxy-auth headers can replace it. Where signed tokens authenticate callers, inspect signature and configured algorithm/key selection, issuer, audience, lifetime and token purpose; token-provided key URLs or identifiers must not become arbitrary lookups or fetches.

validation.method: With disposable identities, compare an allowed request with missing/tampered credentials and spoofed identity headers. For token-based authentication, test wrong issuer/audience/purpose, expired, disallowed-algorithm or unsigned/untrusted-key tokens and conflicting credential sources; assert the effective principal and protected operation, not only a response code. Exercise trusted-proxy identity assertions through their actual configured boundary; use local keys/mocks and no external key fetch.
evidence_required: Protected-entry inventory and executed cases linking credential source, verified principal and denied operation; distinguish configured provider guarantees from exercised application behavior.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Public endpoints and authenticated proxy assertions can be intentional. JWT checks apply only to the token mechanism in use; client Origin, IP address or a decoded claim is not itself authentication.

controls.title: Registration and linking
controls.expected_outcome: Registration, invitations and account linking cannot join an unintended identity.

research.method: Trace signup, invitations and identity linking to the provider subject and verified account. Inspect binding to the initiating session, intended recipient and provider. Where OAuth/OIDC is used, inspect callback registration, state/nonce/PKCE protections as applicable and issuer/token-type separation; do not link identities solely because an unverified email or caller-supplied subject matches.

validation.method: Use disposable accounts to pair valid signup/linking with swapped invitation recipients, tampered provider/subject claims and replayed or cross-session callbacks. Exercise mismatched redirect/state/nonce or proof-key cases where applicable. Assert no unintended account creation, merge, session replacement or invitation use; mocked providers do not establish live provider configuration.
evidence_required: Account/link identity mapping before and after each authorized case, including session/provider binding and remaining provider-side evidence gaps.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Owner-approved linking after suitable reauthentication may be valid. A matching display name or email alone does not establish either a legitimate identity match or a proven takeover.

controls.title: Credential and recovery controls
controls.expected_outcome: Passwords, OTPs, magic links and recovery credentials have appropriate expiry and replay controls.

research.method: Inspect password/OTP/magic-link/recovery verification, attempt controls and server-side lifetime. Trace one-time credentials to their intended account, action and channel; inspect whether client timestamps, account selectors or a token issued for another purpose can change validation. Keep token trust checks aligned with B-01 and account linking with B-02.

validation.method: In approved fixtures, pair a valid credential use with expired, reused, wrong-account and wrong-purpose credentials, including configured clock boundaries and bounded failed attempts. Check that recovery failures create no session or account change and that successful one-time credentials cannot be reused. Never collect usable production tokens or flood a provider.
evidence_required: Credential lifetime/purpose configuration and synthetic execution results showing session/account state and one-time consumption without retaining usable secrets.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Apply the mechanism actually deployed; do not impose password-specific rules on passwordless systems or infer weakness solely from a provider-managed flow.

controls.title: Authentication abuse
controls.expected_outcome: Enumeration, automated authentication/enrollment abuse and cheap-account amplification are constrained without relying on client controls.

research.method: Inspect responses, throttles, counters and anti-automation configuration. Include registration, recovery and provider-delegated flows where present; assess account-creation cost, aggregate quotas and whether fresh accounts reset downstream budgets. Distinguish Auth endpoint throttles from database/storage/realtime workload protection under F-08.

validation.method: Perform bounded approved negative tests without flooding production. Use disposable identities or a bounded provider mock to test repeated enrollment/recovery, budget resets across identities and a legitimate signup/login neighbor. Confirm downstream exposure separately; do not create bulk live accounts or assume a CAPTCHA/provider throttle protects data APIs.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Public registration/recovery must work without an existing sign-in. Service-only authentication need not invent signup. No specific CAPTCHA or identity-proofing product is mandatory; establish effective abuse bounds and disclose provider evidence gaps.

controls.title: Session lifecycle
controls.expected_outcome: Expiry, refresh, revocation, logout and direct identity changes preserve the intended principal across clients and in-flight work.

research.method: Trace session state, refresh, persistence and revocation, including direct A-to-B identity switching without logout. Inspect ownership/epoch binding of delayed requests and refresh callbacks; online in-flight work is relevant even when no offline queue exists. Queued-write retention is additionally covered by M-04. Trace the actual enforcement point and maximum propagation delay for blocking a principal or revoking a session, including unexpired tokens, caches, open subscriptions and pending work. Refresh-token invalidation alone may leave access tokens usable; reconcile the containment deadline with O-04.

validation.method: With disposable sessions, pair normal same-account refresh/reconnect with logout, expiry, revocation and direct A-to-B switching while an A response or refresh is delayed. Assert a late A result cannot restore A credentials, display A data to B or change B authority. Previously authorized A work may complete only under its original attribution and declared policy; do not require indiscriminate cancellation or erase retained work. With a disposable unexpired token and established connection, block/revoke the designated identity and measure when access and ongoing work stop under the declared policy; verify a different legitimate principal remains usable. State cache/stream/pending-work limits and distinguish refresh denial from current access denial.
evidence_required: Ordered principal/session transition and delayed-response/refresh observations, with final visible and persisted identity and no usable token material.
Declared containment deadline and observed access/connection behavior using a previously issued unexpired credential; no usable token material retained.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Static service credentials need not implement browser sessions. Safe same-account refresh and explicitly attributed completion of earlier work are not defects; establish a wrong-principal effect or lifecycle-policy violation.

controls.title: Token confidentiality
controls.expected_outcome: Credentials and tokens do not leak through unsafe storage, URLs, logs or analytics.

research.method: Inspect storage choices, redirects, telemetry and redacted request metadata.

validation.method: Check controlled login flows and artifacts without capturing usable credentials.

controls.title: Privileged authentication
controls.expected_outcome: Privileged accounts have suitable MFA, recovery and emergency-access controls.

research.method: Inspect authorized administrative authentication policy and recovery documentation.

validation.method: Confirm effective settings and recovery ownership without changing access.

controls.title: Sensitive account operations
controls.expected_outcome: Email changes, deletion and recovery enforce appropriate identity verification and cleanup.

research.method: Inspect sensitive action authorization, reauthentication and lifecycle handlers.

validation.method: Test only approved account lifecycle cases with disposable identities.

controls.title: Role matrix
controls.expected_outcome: Anonymous, user, service and administrative permissions are explicit.

research.method: Map roles to resources and operations in code and policy.

validation.method: Reconcile the matrix with endpoint and data-layer checks.

controls.title: Ownership enforcement
controls.expected_outcome: Reads, writes, deletes, downloads and exports enforce resource ownership.

research.method: Inspect ownership predicates on all operation paths.

validation.method: Compare owner and non-owner behavior using approved synthetic resources.

controls.title: Object and tenant isolation
controls.expected_outcome: Changing identifiers cannot cross account or tenant boundaries.

research.method: Trace resource lookups, joins, caches and indirect operations to server-verified tenant/account context. Compare route, query, body and header identifiers, repeated or conflicting selectors and nested parent/child relationships. A valid identifier or tenant header must not itself grant ownership; identify intentional delegated cross-tenant operations.

validation.method: Use two disposable identities and known synthetic resources. Pair owner access with another tenant identifier in each accepted location, conflicting header/body contexts and mismatched parent/child IDs. Assert returned fields, writes and side effects remain within the authorized scope, including indirect operations; a single successful owner request proves no isolation.
evidence_required: Identity-to-resource matrix and before/after state or response evidence for allowed and cross-boundary cases, with delegated permissions stated.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Public resources and explicitly authorized service/delegation access are not automatically leaks. Prove the principal/resource boundary rather than flagging every client-selected ID.

controls.title: Field-level authorization
controls.expected_outcome: Client input cannot assign protected fields or escalate privileges.

research.method: Inspect operation-specific field allowlists, serializers, bulk/nested updates and data policies. Trace protected role, owner, tenant, price and approval fields through defaulting, merge/patch and alternate encodings; inspect dynamic object merges for prototype-sensitive writes. Field shape validation and authorization are separate decisions.

validation.method: Pair an allowed field update with protected or unknown fields, nested/bulk forms, explicit null/unset and duplicate/conflicting representations supported by the stack. Assert protected fields and authorization context remain unchanged. For relevant object runtimes, use bounded prototype-key fixtures and inspect only disposable objects; field stripping is acceptable when it prevents the effect.
evidence_required: Allowed/protected-field contract, actual deserializer/update path and persisted before/after assertions for both allowed and denied edits.

controls.false_positive_guidance: An ignored field, legitimate administrator edit or a prototype-like key stored as inert data is not itself escalation. Demonstrate assignment into protected state or a harmful merge target.

controls.title: Delegation and administration
controls.expected_outcome: Promotion, support access, impersonation and delegation are narrowly authorized and attributable.

research.method: Review admin checks, delegation lifecycle and audit events.

validation.method: Validate role changes and revocation with designated test roles.

controls.title: Indirect authorization
controls.expected_outcome: Jobs, exports, bulk actions and nested resources retain authorization context.

research.method: Trace queued work and indirect resource access.

validation.method: Test an authorized and unauthorized indirect operation in isolation.

controls.title: Shared access lifecycle
controls.expected_outcome: Shared links and invitations have appropriate scope, expiry and revocation.

research.method: Inspect link tokens, scopes, reuse and revocation paths.

validation.method: Verify expiry and access removal without exposing real shared data.

controls.title: Derived-data isolation
controls.expected_outcome: Caches, indexes and live subscriptions preserve access boundaries.

research.method: Inspect cache keys, index filters, event payloads and subscription policies.

validation.method: Check cross-identity retrieval and subscription cases with synthetic data.

controls.title: Data-surface inventory
controls.expected_outcome: Exposed schemas, tables, views, functions, buckets and publications have intentional access and identified abuse-enforcement boundaries.

research.method: Inspect migrations, grants, API exposure configuration and authorized catalog metadata. Map tables/views, RPC/functions, storage and publications to every API/transport that exposes them, including provider-generated and alternate APIs. Record intended anonymous/authenticated access, effective resource bounds and enforcement ownership with F-08; check defaults for newly created objects and whether pre-request hooks cover each product, method and read path.

validation.method: Reconcile live metadata with intended public/private surfaces and the surface-to-enforcement matrix. In an authorized isolated fixture, verify representative newly exposed objects and alternate paths cannot escape required protection. Preserve unknown provider settings as evidence requests; a policy name alone does not prove enforcement.
evidence_required: Surface-to-enforcement matrix linking object, operation, ingress, access policy, resource budget, enforcement point and provider/product limitations.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Public reads and correctly scoped direct data access can be intentional. RLS/grants establish access boundaries, not automatically rate limits; database-only or storage-only projects need not invent absent products.

controls.title: Row-level isolation
controls.expected_outcome: Data authorization remains effective for each operation supported by the storage model.

research.method: Inspect RLS or equivalent data-layer policies, including inserts and checks.

validation.method: Test anonymous and cross-owner operations using synthetic records.

controls.title: Database privileges
controls.expected_outcome: Roles, grants, default privileges and function execution follow least privilege.

research.method: Inspect grants and authorized metadata without reading private rows.

validation.method: Compare effective privileges for public, user and service roles.

controls.title: Privileged database code
controls.expected_outcome: Elevated functions enforce callers and use safe resolution rules.

research.method: Inspect elevated database routines, ownership, grants, search-path/object resolution and caller checks. Trace dynamic query values and identifiers inside functions, including routines callable through APIs; calling a stored procedure does not establish safe construction or suitable execution privilege.

validation.method: In an approved isolated database, pair an allowed call with unauthorized callers, cross-owner arguments, injected dynamic identifier/value fixtures and hostile object resolution where supported. Assert returned rows and state, and confirm intended execution privileges; do not create shadow objects or alter grants in a live database.
evidence_required: Routine definitions and effective execution context tied to allowed/denied call results and affected rows or state in the declared database fixture.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Elevated routines can be legitimate when callers, resolution and reachable effects are constrained. Establish an unsafe path; the presence of elevated execution syntax alone is not a defect.

controls.title: Views and derived relations
controls.expected_outcome: Views and other derived relations do not bypass expected isolation.

research.method: Inspect view security mode, ownership and relation grants.

validation.method: Compare derived-resource visibility across test identities.

controls.title: Database encryption and access
controls.expected_outcome: Sensitive stored data and backups have appropriate encryption and key protection; direct connections require suitable authentication and verified encrypted transport.

research.method: Review transport and at-rest encryption, backup protection, key access/lifecycle, network controls and credential distribution.

validation.method: Verify effective settings using authorized metadata; do not scan networks.

controls.title: Object storage authorization
controls.expected_outcome: Listing, upload, download and signed URLs have intentional scope and expiry.

research.method: Inspect bucket visibility, storage policies and URL issuance.

validation.method: Test allowed and denied operations with disposable objects.

controls.title: Database integrity
controls.expected_outcome: Constraints, relationships, orphan handling and cascades preserve consistency and privacy.

research.method: Inspect constraints, deletion behavior and aggregate integrity queries.

validation.method: Use read-only aggregates or isolated fixtures to confirm integrity.

controls.title: Interpreter injection
controls.expected_outcome: Untrusted input cannot become executable query, command, template or expression syntax.

research.method: Map request, stored and third-party values to SQL/ORM raw queries, dynamic procedures, NoSQL operators, LDAP/XPath queries, subprocesses and template/evaluation sinks that actually exist. Inspect value binding separately from allowed identifiers and sort directions; trace stored values reused in later queries. For processes, inspect executable resolution, shell use, argument boundaries and option injection. Validation or manual escaping alone does not establish safe interpreter use.

validation.method: Pair a legitimate value containing punctuation with inert syntax-like input through the real query builder/driver or isolated interpreter fixture. Check query structure, bound values and resulting row/tenant scope; include raw-query escapes, dynamic identifiers, stored-input reuse and operator-shaped objects where relevant. For processes, use a harmless argument recorder to verify one data argument cannot become an option or another command. For templates, verify input remains data. No destructive SQL, delays, file extraction or live command execution.
evidence_required: Input-to-sink matrix with actual adapter/interpreter versions, case inputs, query/argument structure and protected-result assertions; identify absent families and untested paths.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Quotes, an ORM call or a suspicious string alone do not prove injection. Parameterized syntax-like data and application-owned identifiers can be valid; establish changed execution meaning or unauthorized effect.

controls.title: Browser script injection
controls.expected_outcome: Untrusted data cannot execute scripts through stored, reflected or DOM rendering.

research.method: Trace stored/reflected/DOM data to HTML, attribute, script, URL and DOM-construction contexts, including framework escape hatches and post-render updates. Inspect the encoder or safe sink for each context rather than relying on a global filter or CSP alone.

validation.method: Render legitimate special characters and inert adversarial markers through the actual component/template in an isolated browser or representative renderer. Exercise relevant attribute, URL and DOM contexts; assert data cannot create executable nodes, handlers or navigation. Preserve raw and rendered observations. Never persist attack content in production or treat absent execution in a plain-string unit test as full browser proof.
evidence_required: Source-to-render-context map with real renderer configuration and positive/negative DOM or output assertions, identifying browser behavior not exercised.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Literal markup displayed as text is safe; intended trusted HTML is not automatically cross-user XSS. Establish writer authority, recipient context and executable interpretation.

controls.title: Rich-content safety
controls.expected_outcome: Markdown, SVG, rich text and generated HTML have context-appropriate sanitization.

research.method: Inspect Markdown/SVG/rich-text/generated-HTML sanitizers, URL-scheme policy and transformations after sanitization. Trace alternate writers and email templates to actual recipients, including generated content; inspect whether allowed content becomes unsafe after reparsing or reinsertion.

validation.method: Through real isolated templates/renderers, pair permitted rich content with inert forbidden-element, handler, encoded-scheme and post-transform fixtures. Assert supported formatting still works and prohibited behavior remains absent after the final transformation. For email, use rendered artifacts or a mocked transport and establish the writer-to-recipient boundary; browser execution rules alone do not describe every mail client.
evidence_required: Sanitizer/version/policy and final-render observations for legitimate and disallowed content, including writer/recipient scope and unsupported clients.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Self-authored markup or an unescaped string does not by itself demonstrate cross-user injection. Policy intentionally permitting bounded rich content need not strip all HTML.

controls.title: Email injection
controls.expected_outcome: Untrusted input cannot add headers, recipients or executable email markup.

research.method: Trace sender, recipient, subject and body inputs through the actual mail library and envelope construction. Inspect CR/LF handling, recipient-list parsing, caller-controlled From/Reply-To and final template escaping; separate transport headers from display names and envelope recipients.

validation.method: Use a captured mocked transport to pair valid names, Unicode and addresses with newline, extra-recipient and sender-override attempts. Assert exact envelope recipients/sender, unchanged header count and safe rendered body. Do not send unsolicited mail; any test inbox needs explicit approval. Email-domain anti-spoof policy is separate from proving safe message construction.
evidence_required: Sanitized captured envelope, structured headers and rendered message for positive and negative cases; no real recipient data or usable credentials.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Library rejection or a safely quoted display name may be correct. Reply-To and delegated senders can be intentional; establish an unauthorized envelope/header change rather than unusual punctuation.

controls.title: Header and redirect trust
controls.expected_outcome: Client-supplied headers cannot forge trusted proxy context, poison generated URLs, or bypass validated redirect destinations.

research.method: Map the actual proxy hops and origin reachability. Trace Host/:authority, Forwarded, X-Forwarded-Host/Proto/For and deployment-specific rewrite/client-IP headers to generated links, secure-request decisions, rate limits and redirects. Verify which peers may assert metadata and how client values are removed or replaced, including conflicting chains and direct-origin access. Inspect redirect parsing after decoding, including scheme, host, port, userinfo and relative forms. Authentication claims belong to B-01.

validation.method: In an approved local chain, pair a legitimate trusted-proxy request with forged host, scheme, client-IP and rewrite headers from an untrusted peer; include conflicting repeated values and direct-origin requests where reachable. Assert generated links, routing, security decisions and rate-limit identity are not attacker-selected. Use synthetic recovery links, not sent mail. Test redirect suffix/lookalike hosts, scheme-relative URLs, backslashes and encoded separators, plus CR/LF attempts; verify the final destination and absence of injected response fields.
evidence_required: Proxy trust/topology configuration and positive/negative observations of effective host, scheme, peer identity, route and redirect target; do not infer deployed trust from a bare handler fixture.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Forwarded metadata is legitimate when asserted by an authenticated or constrained trusted hop and unreachable for client forgery. Merely reflecting an inert host string is not proof of a crossed security boundary.

controls.title: Server-side request safety
controls.expected_outcome: Outbound requests cannot access unintended hosts, networks, schemes or redirect targets.

research.method: Trace user, stored and third-party destinations through URL parsing, DNS resolution, redirects and the actual connector. Inspect schemes, userinfo, ports, host comparison, IPv4/IPv6 and address representations; connect to the destination that was checked. Revalidate redirect hops and prevent credential forwarding across trust boundaries. Inspect private/loopback/link-local and metadata destinations where relevant, including proxy bypasses.

validation.method: Use deterministic resolver/connector stubs or an isolated controlled server. Pair an allowed destination with misleading host suffixes, userinfo, disallowed schemes/ports, private-address variants, changed DNS answers and redirects into a forbidden target. Assert the selected connection and forwarded credentials, not just URL acceptance. Never probe real internal services, metadata endpoints or arbitrary domains.
evidence_required: Parsed and resolved destination, redirect chain and connector-call observations for allowed/denied cases, separating stubbed results from actual network enforcement.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Intended internal-service calls or an authenticated proxy may be allowed. A supplied URL alone is not SSRF; demonstrate a reachable forbidden connection under the stated policy.

controls.title: File and parser boundaries
controls.expected_outcome: Paths, archives, deserializers and parsers cannot escape intended boundaries or exhaust resources.

research.method: Inspect normalization and confinement for paths/archives, including encoded separators, absolute paths, symlinks and extraction targets. Inventory actual JSON/XML/YAML/object parsers and deserializers; inspect external entity/network access, executable object construction and bounds on depth, expansion and decompression before work is allocated.

validation.method: Use disposable directories and bounded malformed/traversal/archive fixtures plus a legitimate confined file. For active parser families, check external access through deny-all stubs, harmless object-construction markers and small depth/expansion limit-plus-one cases. Assert no escape, unexpected constructor or external call and bounded resource use. No real secrets, executable gadgets or resource bombs.
evidence_required: Final resolved paths, parser configuration and observable filesystem/network/construction effects with measured bounds; record families absent from the actual stack.

controls.false_positive_guidance: A filename containing punctuation, an inert serialized key or a parser supporting rich syntax is not enough. Identify an enabled unsafe behavior or a confinement/resource failure.

controls.title: Upload safety
controls.expected_outcome: Uploads cannot create unintended executable hosting or bypass content and size restrictions.

research.method: Trace upload filename, claimed MIME type and bytes through validation, parsing, storage and retrieval. Inspect extension/content-policy consistency, untrusted serving origin/headers, authorization, quotas and expansion limits; file signatures alone do not establish harmless content.

validation.method: In a designated disposable store, pair a permitted file with bounded extension/MIME/content mismatches, active-content markers, traversal names and size/count limit-plus-one cases. Assert stored location, retrieval headers/origin and authorization, no overwrite or server execution, and rejection/containment according to policy. Use inert mixed-content fixtures, not malware or decompression bombs.
evidence_required: Claimed versus observed file metadata and final storage/serving behavior, linked to allowed and disallowed content and authorization cases.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Intentional arbitrary-file storage served as an isolated attachment can be valid. MIME mismatch alone is not executable hosting; assess the actual retrieval and processing boundary.

controls.title: Endpoint inventory
controls.expected_outcome: Public, provider-generated, legacy, debug and administrative endpoints have intentional exposure and known enforcement paths.

research.method: Inspect route definitions, client SDK destinations, deployment configuration and authorized endpoint metadata. Include direct provider URLs, alternate hostnames/APIs, RPC, auth, storage and realtime handshakes where present. Map methods, intended access, gateway dependence and effective enforcement rather than listing only application-owned routes.

validation.method: Compare deployed surfaces against the inventory without brute-force discovery. For gateway-dependent protection, use an explicitly authorized bounded direct-origin/provider request with ordinary client credentials and missing/forged gateway context; require denial or equivalent protection, and pair it with a legitimate permitted request. Prove downstream work is bounded with F-08, not merely that one URL returned an error.
evidence_required: Ingress/method-to-enforcement mapping and authorized bypass/legitimate-neighbor observations, including alternate provider endpoints and missing evidence.

controls.false_positive_guidance: A gateway is optional when effective protection exists elsewhere. A server-only secret header can contribute to enforcement but a browser-visible value, CORS or hidden URL does not establish non-bypassability.

controls.title: Request contracts
controls.expected_outcome: Input contracts are enforced at trusted boundaries before business effects, and inconsistent parsing cannot bypass them.

research.method: Trace path/query/body/header/cookie inputs through proxy and application parsing, decoding, normalization and server-side validation. Inspect types/coercion, required versus null/missing values, numeric/date bounds, enums, lengths, nested arrays/objects, unknown fields and cross-field invariants. Check repeated parameters/JSON keys, conflicting input sources, media types and limits before buffering/decompression. For deployed HTTP chains, inspect length/transfer framing, duplicate security fields and protocol translation; client validation is insufficient.

validation.method: Use legitimate boundary, Unicode and punctuation cases, then bounded wrong-type, null, missing, out-of-range, unknown-field, nesting and limit-plus-one cases against the real parser/validator. Assert rejected or stripped values cannot reach protected state or downstream work. Test repeated/conflicting values and alternate encodings at security decisions. Exercise malformed framing only in an isolated representative proxy/backend chain with explicit authority; absent chain evidence stays unresolved, not a smuggling pass.
evidence_required: Field/transport contract and case matrix showing parser and normalization order, boundary values, downstream-call/state assertions and which proxy hops were actually exercised.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Documented coercion, ignored fields, free text and repeatable list-valued HTTP fields can be legitimate. Find harmful interpretation differences; do not require universal character blacklists or rejection of every duplicate header.

controls.title: Cross-origin defenses
controls.expected_outcome: CORS and applicable CSRF defenses match the authentication model.

research.method: Inspect actual CORS origin comparison, credential rules, preflight handling and applicable CSRF defenses on state-changing paths. Trace Origin/Referer and fetch metadata through the proxy boundary without treating browser-managed headers as authentication. Include reflected/null origins, suffix/lookalike hosts and unsafe state changes hidden behind nominally safe methods.

validation.method: Use an isolated browser or representative HTTP fixture to pair a permitted origin/request with disallowed and null origins, credentialed requests, missing/wrong-session CSRF tokens and simple cross-site submissions where relevant. Assert readable response and protected state separately; CORS rejection alone does not prove no side effect. Direct non-browser clients must still require authentication/authorization.
evidence_required: Origin/credential/token policy and browser-versus-server observations of response access and state changes, including which attack preconditions apply.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Public noncredentialed resources may allow broad origins. APIs without ambient credentials may not need browser CSRF tokens; justify the actual credential model rather than demanding every mechanism.

controls.title: Security response headers
controls.expected_outcome: Browser security headers provide appropriate protections without breaking essential behavior.

research.method: Inspect response header configuration and third-party script needs.

validation.method: Read effective headers for declared URLs and compare with policy.

controls.title: Secure transport and cookies
controls.expected_outcome: Cookies, redirects and resource loads preserve confidentiality and integrity.

research.method: Inspect cookie attributes, HTTPS enforcement and mixed-content paths.

validation.method: Check authorized browser flows and effective transport configuration.

controls.title: Cache boundaries
controls.expected_outcome: CDN and application caching cannot mix authenticated content or accept poisoned variants.

research.method: Map cache keys and representations across CDN/proxy/application layers. Trace attacker-controlled authority, forwarded headers, origin, query normalization, cookies and identity to response content and cache variation. Inspect authenticated cacheability, poisoning/deception paths and whether unkeyed inputs can change a shared response.

validation.method: Only in a disposable cache namespace, pair legitimate cache hits with alternate-identity requests and host/forwarded/origin/query variants. Prime and retrieve with two synthetic principals; assert no private response reuse or poisoned link/header/body for an uninvolved requester. Verify effective cache hit/key behavior; do not poison shared production caches.
evidence_required: Cache-layer/key policy and ordered prime/retrieve observations proving intended reuse and isolation across principals and request variants.

controls.false_positive_guidance: An unusual header or a cached public response is not automatically poisoning. Establish attacker influence over a reused representation or unauthorized private-content mixing.

controls.title: Live and flexible APIs
controls.expected_outcome: WebSockets, subscriptions, GraphQL and batching retain limits and authorization.

research.method: Trace authentication and schema checks at connection, message, GraphQL resolver and batch-item boundaries. Inspect message types, nested variables, operation allowlists, complexity/batch limits and identity/tenant selectors; connection admission alone does not authorize every later operation. Include subscription revocation and origin checks where relevant.

validation.method: Use synthetic connections/accounts to pair permitted operations with malformed/oversized messages, unexpected fields/types, forged tenant selectors and mixed authorized/unauthorized batch items. Assert each resolver/action and subscription payload respects the principal after logout/revocation, and bounded limits apply before expensive fan-out. Do not stress a live service.
evidence_required: Per-message/resolver/batch case mapping with operation/state/payload assertions, connection lifecycle and measured limits for the actual API protocol.

controls.false_positive_guidance: GraphQL, batching and public subscriptions are not inherently unsafe. Assess permitted operations and actual effects; do not mandate disabling a useful protocol merely because it exists.

controls.title: Resource abuse controls
controls.expected_outcome: Reachable operations constrain per-caller and aggregate resource consumption, scraping and shared-quota exhaustion across every enforcement path.

research.method: Inspect surface-to-enforcement mappings for direct provider access as well as owned endpoints, including reads, writes, RPC, storage, auth and realtime where present. Identify per-principal, trusted peer, concurrency and aggregate budgets, cheap-account/device rotation and shared quota blast radius. Trace limiter keys to verified identities and trusted proxy context, not caller-controlled forwarding/device headers. Inspect pagination, fan-out, regex/parser/decompression work, retries and billable operations; determine what work rejection itself consumes and whether gateway, pre-request and RLS checks cover each product, method and alternate ingress.

validation.method: With mocked costly dependencies or an isolated bounded workload, pair legitimate anonymous/authenticated operations and limit-boundary cases with limit-plus-one, concurrent requests, account/peer rotation and spoofed identity/header variants. Where protection depends on a gateway, try direct provider/alternate ingress without valid gateway context. Measure downstream calls, allocations, elapsed work and aggregate consumption before and after denial; an HTTP error or 429 alone proves no resource bound. Assert rejected work stays within a justified rejection budget and cannot trigger prohibited billable side effects, while another legitimate principal retains the declared service budget. Exercise limiter dependency failure and actual supported read/write/stream boundaries; never flood or stress production.
evidence_required: Justified configured budgets, trustworthy limiter identity and measured positive/negative resource or upstream-call counts under the authorized fixture.

Surface-to-enforcement matrix, trusted limiter identity, per-operation/concurrency/aggregate budgets, measured allowed/rejected downstream work and unaffected-user observations; fixture/provider limitations and limiter-failure behavior stated.

controls.false_positive_guidance: No universal sign-in, gateway, rate-limit product, IP/device identifier or request count is required. Public bounded/cached access and private workload controls may be legitimate. IPs can be shared, devices reset and accounts farmed; authentication or per-user limits alone do not establish shared-resource protection. Establish a credible unbounded path or unknown evidence, and account for equivalent controls and unavoidable bounded rejection costs.

controls.title: Secret exposure
controls.expected_outcome: Source, history, bundles, artifacts and logs contain no unintended sensitive secrets.

research.method: Use scoped redacted secret scanning and inspect artifact construction. Include developer and agent output, PR bodies, attachments, screenshots, fixtures, source maps and reports. Identify credential type and location without reproducing a usable value; public identifiers are not automatically secrets.

validation.method: Confirm candidates by context without printing or attempting to use secrets.

controls.title: Secret lifecycle
controls.expected_outcome: Secrets have controlled storage, scope, rotation and revocation.

research.method: Inspect secret references, environment boundaries and operational procedures. Inspect credential-helper and injection mechanisms, environment isolation, lifetime and incident revocation. Deleting an exposed value from a file is not proof of containment.

validation.method: Verify presence and scope through metadata, never secret-value exports.

controls.title: Administrative access
controls.expected_outcome: Human and service access is least-privileged and stale access is retired.

research.method: Review authorized role inventories and offboarding procedures. Include developer tokens, automation identities, credential ownership and effective repository permissions.

validation.method: Confirm access ownership without granting, revoking or logging into new accounts.

controls.title: Dependency assurance
controls.expected_outcome: Dependencies and assets have known provenance, support status and acceptable licenses.

research.method: Inspect lockfiles, advisories, licenses and dependency sources. Verify dependency identities and actual API existence against installed or pinned versions; detect misleading package names and unsupported generated imports.

validation.method: Reconcile scanner candidates with installed versions and actual reachability.

controls.title: CI trust boundaries
controls.expected_outcome: Untrusted contributions cannot execute privileged workflows or expose build secrets.

research.method: Inspect workflow triggers, permissions, actions and scripts. Include contribution trust, workflow token scope, action pinning, artifact/cache poisoning and privileged follow-up workflows.

validation.method: Use static analysis and isolated workflow fixtures rather than privileged PR execution.

controls.title: Release integrity
controls.expected_outcome: Release inputs, approval boundaries and published artifacts are attributable and controlled.

research.method: Inspect branch policy, build inputs and artifact provenance. Trace backend as well as frontend dependency resolution, direct and transitive identities, retained bundles and actual deploy-tool lock consumption.

validation.method: Compare a declared release with commit and artifact metadata. Compare isolated clean build graphs with retained deployment artifacts; a lockfile that the deploy tool ignores is insufficient.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Floating source imports do not prove a vulnerable SDK or changing live bundle. Retained build artifacts may supply a binding absent from the repository.

controls.title: Environment separation
controls.expected_outcome: Previews, fixtures and debug features cannot unintentionally expose or modify production.

research.method: Inspect environment mappings, test data and debug routes.

validation.method: Compare effective preview/production configuration and document deliberately shared services.

controls.title: Deployment drift
controls.expected_outcome: Deployed versions and configuration match the intended release and policy.

research.method: Compare authorized deployment metadata with source and configuration.

validation.method: Record exact commits, function versions and scoped drift evidence.

controls.title: Processing inventory
controls.expected_outcome: Personal-data processing has defined purposes, recipients, ownership and retention.

research.method: Map fields and processing paths without reading real personal records.

validation.method: Reconcile the inventory against schemas and integrations.

controls.title: Accurate privacy notice
controls.expected_outcome: Published privacy statements match collection, sharing and actual practices.

research.method: Compare notices, code, telemetry and provider documentation.

validation.method: Validate specific promises against implementation and effective settings.

controls.title: Data minimization
controls.expected_outcome: Collection and permissions are limited to documented product purposes.

research.method: Inspect forms, device permissions, identifiers and unused fields.

validation.method: Resolve necessity with the product owner and inspect effective collection.

controls.title: Applicable user rights
controls.expected_outcome: Applicable access, export, correction, deletion and objection processes exist.

research.method: Determine jurisdictional applicability using current primary sources and business facts.

validation.method: Verify applicable requests using designated accounts and approved procedures.

controls.title: Request fulfillment
controls.expected_outcome: Privacy requests are discoverable, verified appropriately and tracked to completion.

research.method: Inspect public entry points, identity checks and operational workflow.

validation.method: Walk through a simulated request without submitting an unauthorized real request.

controls.title: Deletion propagation
controls.expected_outcome: Deletion reaches relevant processors, objects, indexes, caches and scheduled work.

research.method: Trace deletion handlers, contracts and residual-data handling.

validation.method: Use disposable data and verify scoped downstream removal after approval.

controls.title: Retention and restoration
controls.expected_outcome: Retention, holds and backup restoration do not silently defeat deletion commitments.

research.method: Inspect retention jobs, backup handling, holds and restoration procedures.

validation.method: Review evidence of lifecycle enforcement and isolated restore/deletion tests.

controls.title: Processor governance
controls.expected_outcome: Vendor terms, subprocessors, transfers and secondary uses match applicable commitments.

research.method: Inspect current agreements, settings and data destinations.

validation.method: Record unresolved contractual or jurisdiction facts for qualified review.

controls.title: Truthful claims
controls.expected_outcome: Material marketing and product claims have support and match actual capabilities.

research.method: Compare public claims, product behavior and substantiation records.

validation.method: Validate concrete claims and refer unresolved legal interpretation for review.

controls.title: Material disclosures
controls.expected_outcome: Pricing, limitations, operator identity and material terms are clear and accessible.

research.method: Inspect purchase, onboarding, policy and public contact surfaces.

validation.method: Review disclosures in the actual decision context and applicable jurisdictions.

controls.title: Non-deceptive choices
controls.expected_outcome: Interfaces do not mislead users or obstruct informed decisions.

research.method: Inspect urgency, defaults, hidden actions, asymmetric choices and cancellation.

validation.method: Walk through affected flows and separate usability concerns from supported legal claims.

controls.title: Subscription and refund terms
controls.expected_outcome: Trials, renewals, cancellation, refunds and purchase consent match applicable obligations.

research.method: Inspect current primary rules, actual offers, billing terms and cancellation paths.

validation.method: Validate applicability and test designated subscription cases only with authorization.

controls.title: Endorsement integrity
controls.expected_outcome: Testimonials, reviews and sponsorship relationships are authentic and appropriately disclosed.

research.method: Inspect marketing content, incentives and affiliate arrangements.

validation.method: Compare actual arrangements with applicable current guidance.

controls.title: Children and age applicability
controls.expected_outcome: Age targeting and data practices support a documented children-privacy determination.

research.method: Inspect audience, design, distribution, collection and actual-knowledge processes.

validation.method: Resolve applicable parental, retention and notice requirements using current sources.

controls.title: Sector-specific obligations
controls.expected_outcome: Health, finance, education, employment and other sector triggers are identified.

research.method: Map product uses and data to current primary-source applicability criteria.

validation.method: Escalate unresolved applicability to an owner or qualified specialist; do not assume certification.

controls.title: Terms and platform obligations
controls.expected_outcome: Terms, policy updates, consent records and distribution requirements are consistent.

research.method: Inspect terms, versioning, acceptance records and applicable marketplace contracts.

validation.method: Confirm relevant platform and contractual requirements against current sources.

controls.title: Tracking inventory
controls.expected_outcome: Analytics, advertising, pixels, SDKs and local storage are documented.

research.method: Inspect dependencies, network destinations and storage keys.

validation.method: Compare approved runtime observations with the tracking inventory.

controls.title: Consent and opt-out
controls.expected_outcome: Applicable consent and withdrawal choices govern actual processing.

research.method: Inspect defaults, consent state, opt-out propagation and legal applicability.

validation.method: Test designated preferences and verify downstream behavior without activating new tracking.

controls.title: Message classification
controls.expected_outcome: Authentication, service, reminder and promotional communications are correctly classified.

research.method: Inspect actual templates, triggers, audience and purpose.

validation.method: Apply current primary guidance to representative messages and record uncertainty.

controls.title: Email compliance
controls.expected_outcome: Applicable sender, subject, disclosure and unsubscribe requirements are implemented.

research.method: Inspect templates, sender identity and unsubscribe flow.

validation.method: Use a mocked transport or approved inbox to verify applicable requirements.

controls.title: Notification preferences
controls.expected_outcome: Schedules respect opt-ins, quiet hours, time zones and duplicate controls.

research.method: Inspect defaults, preference reads, scheduling and delivery deduplication.

validation.method: Test synthetic recipients across timing and preference boundaries.

controls.title: Delivery authentication
controls.expected_outcome: Sending-domain authentication and delivery failure handling are configured.

research.method: Review public DNS and authorized provider metadata for authentication and suppression.

validation.method: Inspect effective SPF, DKIM, DMARC and controlled delivery evidence.

controls.title: Message confidentiality
controls.expected_outcome: Notifications avoid unintended sensitive content or unsafe bearer links.

research.method: Inspect templates, URL tokens and lock-screen exposure.

validation.method: Review representative synthetic messages and link scope/expiry.

controls.title: Communication cessation
controls.expected_outcome: Deletion, opt-out, suspension and closure stop applicable future communications.

research.method: Trace scheduled recipients, queued sends and suppression state.

validation.method: Test with a designated recipient or mocked queue after explicit scope approval.

controls.title: Trusted amounts
controls.expected_outcome: Trusted systems determine prices, discounts, taxes and payable amounts.

research.method: Inspect purchase calculation, provider calls and client-supplied monetary fields.

validation.method: Test manipulated amounts in provider sandbox or local fixtures.

controls.title: Webhook integrity
controls.expected_outcome: External payment and entitlement events are authenticated, fresh and idempotent.

research.method: Apply the delivery-authenticity method in S-01 to the payment/entitlement provider protocol. Trace verified raw bytes and sender/key context to the intended account, event record and business transition; inspect replay windows, rotation and atomic duplicate handling.

validation.method: Reuse S-01 valid, forged, changed-body, wrong-key/sender and protocol-supported freshness/rotation cases with local signing fixtures. Add wrong-account/event-context and duplicate/concurrent delivery cases; assert invalid deliveries cause no state change or consumer call, while legitimate retries are acknowledged without repeated business effects. Use mocked fulfillment and no real charges, grants or messages.
evidence_required: Provider verification contract and event-to-account/state case matrix, with no-effect assertions for rejected deliveries and idempotent outcomes for valid retries.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Follow the actual provider protocol rather than inventing signed timestamp/ID fields. A duplicate may legitimately receive success without another business effect. Delivery authenticity alone does not prove price, entitlement or reconciliation correctness.

controls.title: Purchase lifecycle
controls.expected_outcome: Failed, cancelled, disputed and refunded purchases have coherent state transitions.

research.method: Trace payment states and exception paths.

validation.method: Exercise provider sandbox cases without making real purchases.

controls.title: Entitlement authority
controls.expected_outcome: Entitlements reflect authoritative payment or grant state and revoke appropriately.

research.method: Inspect provisioning, revocation and access enforcement.

validation.method: Test designated grants and revocations in an isolated environment.

controls.title: Reward and quota abuse
controls.expected_outcome: Credits, XP, coupons, trials and referrals cannot be claimed outside their intended rules.

research.method: Inspect reward calculations, quotas, claim checks and client-controlled values.

validation.method: Use synthetic claims and bounded race fixtures to verify business invariants.

controls.title: Concurrent valuable state
controls.expected_outcome: Duplicate or concurrent actions cannot corrupt balances, inventory or rewards.

research.method: Inspect atomic updates, constraints, transaction boundaries and locks.

validation.method: Run deterministic concurrency tests with disposable state.

controls.title: Reconciliation
controls.expected_outcome: Partial financial or valuable-state failures can be detected and reconciled.

research.method: Inspect audit records, settlement, reconciliation and repair procedures.

validation.method: Review isolated failure scenarios and evidence of reconciliation.

controls.title: Payment data scope
controls.expected_outcome: Payment-data handling and provider obligations are understood and minimized.

research.method: Trace card/payment data and inspect provider integration boundaries.

validation.method: Confirm applicable provider and security obligations with current authoritative evidence.

controls.title: AI system inventory
controls.expected_outcome: Models, tools, sources, settings and transmitted information are inventoried.

research.method: Inspect prompts, provider calls, retrieval sources and tool declarations.

validation.method: Reconcile declared AI paths with effective configuration and approved observations.

controls.title: Prompt injection boundaries
controls.expected_outcome: Untrusted content cannot redefine authority or silently expand an AI task.

research.method: Trace user, document, retrieval and tool-result content into privileged decisions.

validation.method: Use isolated adversarial fixtures with inert tools and no real external effects.

controls.title: Tool authority
controls.expected_outcome: Automated actions have bounded permissions and appropriate approval requirements.

research.method: Inspect tool allowlists, credentials, confirmation gates and delegation. Include coding-agent credential access, cancellation, denied-action handling and authority separation. Retrieved instructions cannot expand authorization.

validation.method: Test disallowed actions with mocked tools; do not perform the real action.

controls.title: AI data confidentiality
controls.expected_outcome: AI processing does not violate access boundaries or data-use commitments.

research.method: Inspect payload minimization, retrieval filters, provider terms and retention settings. Include source, logs and credential references transmitted by coding agents or external model tools.

validation.method: Test synthetic cross-user retrieval and reconcile documented provider practices.

controls.title: Output safety and claims
controls.expected_outcome: Generated output is safely rendered and appropriate for its product use, including physical safety, consent, age/ability suitability and avoidance of harmful or illegal recommendations where relevant.

research.method: Inspect output handling, unsupported claims, dangerous activity, trespass, harassment, nonconsensual interactions and suitability constraints relevant to the product.

validation.method: Use representative and adversarial offline evaluations with explicit acceptance criteria.

controls.title: Output integrity
controls.expected_outcome: Truncated, malformed or partial AI output cannot leave inconsistent business data.

research.method: Inspect schemas, stop reasons, persistence boundaries and retry behavior.

validation.method: Test malformed, truncated and duplicate responses with mocked providers.

controls.title: AI resource controls
controls.expected_outcome: AI calls have bounded budgets, concurrency, retries and failure handling.

research.method: Inspect token limits, loops, spend controls, provider timeouts and quotas.

validation.method: Test bounded mocked failures and budget enforcement without paid runaway calls.

controls.title: AI lifecycle assurance
controls.expected_outcome: Safety reporting, escalation and evaluations respond to model or prompt changes.

research.method: Inspect evaluation sets, reporting routes, monitoring and version-change procedures.

validation.method: Review evaluation evidence and owner decisions for the deployed model/prompt version.

controls.title: Idempotent operations
controls.expected_outcome: Repeated important actions do not produce duplicate business effects.

research.method: Trace intent/operation keys from client or scheduler through persistence and external consumers, including retries after an ambiguous result. Inspect deduplication lifetime, payload/account binding and concurrent duplicate handling; a new transport attempt is not automatically a new business intent.

validation.method: In an isolated fixture, compare one successful operation, the same intent retried after its commit/acceptance response is lost, and concurrent duplicate attempts. Assert one intended business effect and a recoverable stored outcome; reject conflicting payload/account reuse where required. A genuinely new intent with a new key must still work. Do not infer completion from a timeout, generic error or missing acknowledgment.
evidence_required: Intent/key-to-effect case matrix with committed state, retry/concurrency observations and a legitimate distinct-operation neighbor.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Not every operation requires exactly-once transport delivery. Establish the business invariant and intended retry contract; a repeated acknowledgment without a repeated effect may be correct.

controls.title: Atomic failure handling
controls.expected_outcome: Partial operations preserve invariants or have explicit compensation and reconciliation.

research.method: Trace transaction/side-effect boundaries and the durable records used to resolve an uncertain outcome. Separate failure before commit, commit followed by a lost response, and downstream partial completion; inspect recovery lookup, idempotent retry, compensation and reconciliation rather than assuming a client error means nothing committed.

validation.method: Inject bounded failures before commit, after commit but before acknowledgment, and between isolated downstream effects. Query durable state independently before retry or compensation, and assert the chosen policy preserves acknowledged and newly committed work. Exercise restart/recovery with retained operation identity; no duplicate effect, orphaned state or false success/failure claim may be hidden by retrying. A successful operation with an ordinary response remains the positive neighbor.
evidence_required: Failure-point diagram and before/after durable state, returned outcome, retry/compensation decisions and unresolved downstream effects for each authorized fixture.

controls.false_positive_guidance: A distributed operation may use explicit reconciliation instead of one transaction. A lost response is not itself data corruption; prove the state/recovery invariant or unsupported completion claim.

controls.title: Concurrent updates
controls.expected_outcome: Stale writes and concurrent changes follow an explicit conflict policy.

research.method: Inspect revision checks, optimistic state and serialization. Trace older retained writes against both newer still-pending and newer already-acknowledged peer writes. Inspect scalar, precise-index and full-column conflicts and session boundaries.

validation.method: Run deterministic two-client conflict tests with disposable records. Use two-client synthetic sequences: fail A, acknowledge newer B, retry A. Cover permanent/transient errors, same/different fields and an explicit conflict policy without discarding unsaved work.

controls.title: Offline and session recovery
controls.expected_outcome: Queued writes remain attributable and recover safely across reload, abandonment and account changes.

research.method: Trace retained writes, reads, caches and retry ownership across offline/reload/abandonment and identity transitions. Explicitly inspect direct A-to-B switching without an intervening logout; bind queued intents, delayed responses and credentials to their original principal and session epoch.

validation.method: Queue or start work as disposable account A, delay its response, then switch directly to B without logout before completion or retry. Test reload and replay in that state. Assert A data cannot appear in B views and A work cannot be applied using B authority or silently relabeled; retain or explicitly resolve A pending work without discarding it. A normal same-account reconnect/retry remains valid. Use real relevant queue/session boundaries or state clearly what is only mocked.
evidence_required: Ordered account/session/queue timeline with request ownership, credentials selected, visible/persisted state and retained-work disposition before and after direct switching.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Pausing an old account queue or requiring reauthentication may be intentional. Do not demand silent replay or discard merely to empty a queue; distinguish user-approved abandonment from accidental work loss.

controls.title: Time semantics
controls.expected_outcome: Dates, time zones, daylight saving, recurrence and expiry use consistent rules.

research.method: Compare client, backend, database and scheduler time calculations.

validation.method: Run boundary fixtures around midnight, DST and year transitions.

controls.title: Background completion
controls.expected_outcome: Jobs and queues track downstream completion, retries and terminal failures.

research.method: Inspect scheduling, delivery, acknowledgments, dead letters and response correlation. Trace customer and operations jobs separately. Establish schedule, logical notification identity, retry-versus-reminder semantics and provider acceptance versus final delivery.

validation.method: Test mocked failure paths and inspect approved historical execution evidence. Use inert partial-success, accepted-but-response-lost, timeout and duplicate-invocation fixtures with bounded retries and defined cadence. Do not assume exactly-once inbox delivery.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Repeated reminders can be intentional. Establish cadence and retry requirements before requiring durable identity or exactly-once behavior.

controls.title: Large-data correctness
controls.expected_outcome: Pagination, bulk operations and error handling do not silently omit or misrepresent data.

research.method: Trace enumeration, cursors, default/hard API page limits, batching and aggregation across each independent source. Check termination, stable ordering, duplicate/missing IDs, empty/error branches and truthful partial-result accounting. Required coverage does not depend on the current dataset already exceeding a limit; aggregate before applying a final ranking limit.

validation.method: Use bounded datasets just below, at and above the actual API/default page or batch limit, with the only eligible record on a later/final page. Exercise independent paginated sources and fail a later page; no incomplete result may be labeled complete. Compare IDs, counts, aggregates and rankings with an independently constructed full-data oracle. Include the legitimate one-page/empty result and verify retries/resumption do not duplicate or silently skip records.
evidence_required: Actual API/page-limit contract, requested cursors/batches, full-data oracle and observed IDs/counts/partial-status metadata, including a failed later page.

controls.false_positive_guidance: An intentional scoped limit or approximate result can be legitimate when accurately represented and consistent with requirements. Do not call a partial response corrupt solely because it is partial; challenge a false completeness claim or missing required data.

controls.title: Dependency failure recovery
controls.expected_outcome: Timeouts, cancellation and outages have recoverable degraded behavior.

research.method: Inspect dependency calls, retry policies, circuit breakers and user recovery. Include cancellation, bounded retries and dependency-specific partial failure rather than relying on indefinite loading or blanket retries.

validation.method: Use isolated fault injection and verify recovery without losing acknowledged work.

controls.title: Keyboard and focus
controls.expected_outcome: Essential functions support keyboard access and coherent focus behavior.

research.method: Inspect interactive semantics, focus order, dialogs and visible focus.

validation.method: Perform scoped keyboard tests on representative flows.

controls.title: Accessible semantics
controls.expected_outcome: Labels, roles, state changes and errors are available to assistive technology.

research.method: Inspect accessibility trees, form associations and announcements.

validation.method: Test named WCAG criteria with appropriate manual and automated evidence.

controls.title: Visual adaptation
controls.expected_outcome: Contrast, reflow, zoom, motion and non-color cues support intended users.

research.method: Inspect styles, layout behavior and motion preferences. Inspect decorative infinite animations, particles and preference-change handling; aria-hidden does not suppress visible motion.

validation.method: Test stated WCAG criteria at relevant zoom and viewport settings. Compare normal and reduced-motion settings on synthetic representative surfaces while preserving essential status feedback.

controls.false_positive_guidance: A motion observation does not establish full accessibility nonconformance or a flashing-threshold violation.

controls.title: Device interaction
controls.expected_outcome: Touch targets, gestures, orientation and supported browsers retain essential behavior.

research.method: Inspect responsive rules, gesture alternatives and support policy.

validation.method: Exercise a declared device/browser matrix with scoped evidence.

controls.title: First-use and denied states
controls.expected_outcome: Onboarding, loading, empty and denied-permission states provide usable next steps.

research.method: Inspect first-use branches and permission-dependent features.

validation.method: Walk through synthetic first-use, empty and denied states.

controls.title: Functional completeness
controls.expected_outcome: Links, controls, routes and content behave as represented.

research.method: Inspect navigation, placeholders, unreachable features and obsolete content. Trace visible success through persistence and downstream completion; detect placeholders, fake counters and controls that silently do nothing.

validation.method: Exercise scoped user journeys without committing real purchases or communications.

controls.title: Understandable recovery
controls.expected_outcome: Errors are plain-language and offer appropriate retry, cancel and work preservation.

research.method: Inspect error mapping, cancellation and form/progress persistence.

validation.method: Use isolated failures and confirm recovery without technical jargon or trapped flows.

controls.title: Essential user controls
controls.expected_outcome: Support, privacy, account, harmful-content reporting and other essential product actions remain discoverable and usable where applicable.

research.method: Inspect settings, help and lifecycle navigation across supported states.

validation.method: Walk through designated essential tasks and record friction or inaccessible actions.

controls.title: Actionable monitoring
controls.expected_outcome: Availability, latency, abuse, cost and silent business failures have actionable detection before shared resource budgets are exhausted.

research.method: Inspect dashboards, thresholds, delivery paths and alert ownership for request rates, concurrency, rejected work, database/resource saturation, quota headroom, egress and provider charges where used. Reconcile detection and response latency with the fastest credible exhaustion path; billing totals or delayed alerts alone may be insufficient.

validation.method: Review historical evidence or approved synthetic alert fixtures for approaching quota/budget exhaustion and notification failure. Verify routing, responsible owner and detection-to-response timing without sending unsolicited messages or consuming live quotas; distinguish a configured rule from delivered actionable evidence.
evidence_required: Budget/threshold-to-owner mapping, headroom and delivery/response timing with provider reporting delay and untested paths disclosed.

controls.false_positive_guidance: Offline libraries or services without metered dependencies need proportionate diagnostics, not invented billing alerts. Alerts detect exposure; they do not enforce limits or prove containment.

controls.title: Safe audit records
controls.expected_outcome: Logs are useful, access-controlled, redacted and retained intentionally.

research.method: Inspect logging statements, sinks, access policies and retention. Include tooling output and build logs; preserve useful redacted evidence without retaining usable credentials.

validation.method: Review redacted samples and synthetic events without exporting private logs.

controls.title: Recovery readiness
controls.expected_outcome: Backups, restores and rollbacks have evidence against documented recovery objectives.

research.method: Inspect backup configuration, recovery targets and restore/rollback records.

validation.method: Use approved isolated recovery exercises; never restore over live production by default.

controls.title: Incident response
controls.expected_outcome: Incidents have ownership, escalation, applicable notification procedures and proportionate tested containment and recovery.

research.method: Inspect runbooks, contacts and current legal/contractual triggers. For exposed or shared services, trace selective principal/peer containment, propagation deadlines, adjustable limits and overload behavior, including stale tokens, caches, alternate ingress, active streams and pending jobs. Record authority, rollback and recovery; read-only mode cannot contain expensive reads and site-wide pause/key rotation may affect every user.

validation.method: Run a tabletop and authorized isolated containment/recovery fixtures where relevant: block one abusive principal or trustworthy peer context, tighten limits, exercise declared degraded/read-only behavior and restore service. Measure the containment deadline using an unexpired token/active connection and pair it with an unaffected legitimate principal. Test the remaining read path and alternate ingress; preserve or explicitly resolve pending legitimate work. Record tabletop-only or unavailable runtime evidence as remaining validation rather than a tested kill switch.
evidence_required: Runbook with accountable operator, precise switch coverage, measured or unresolved propagation deadline, collateral effects, authorized fixture outcomes and recovery/rollback observations.

controls.false_positive_guidance: No universal device identity, zero-delay global revocation, read-only switch or particular gateway is required. Use risk-justified containment and recovery objectives; global shutdown may be an explicit last resort but does not establish selective protection. Local-only tools need proportionate response procedures.

controls.title: Operational continuity
